subject: Request: runtime filter exclusion & monitoring agreement for FinPay integration
messages:
From: Liz Harrison <liz@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finpay.com, security@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for filter-triggered toolcall failures

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from the FinPay integration team — over the past two weeks we've observed a string of timeouts when our payments orchestration triggers the structured-output toolchain. Most incidents correlate with content-policy checks that run synchronously before the tool-call. When the policy check spikes, the downstream tool-call times out and our customers see an error flow.

We understand content checks are part of Redwood's safeguards, but for our high-throughput payment flows we need a narrowly scoped operational exception: allow the tool-call to proceed (with asynchronous policy audit) when the policy-check latency exceeds X ms, and have that behavior explicitly excluded from the standard 99.9% per-request latency SLA for a transit window.

Can you share:
- Whether Redwood can support a scoped SLA amendment/exclusion for these filter-triggered failures.
- Proposed acceptance criteria and monitoring (how will FinPay be notified, what metrics will we see).
- Suggested mitigation steps and rollback triggers.

We're open to a time-limited exemption while we implement cached verdicts / async rescoring on our side, but need formal language for procurement and security.

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Harrison
Head of Integrations, FinPay Inc.
Attachment: incident_log_20270531.csv (text/csv, 47KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harrison <liz@finpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for filter-triggered toolcall failures

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear summary and the incident log. I pulled this into the account thread and looped in Ben (SE) and Karthik (security) so we can triage both the operational and compliance sides.

High level: Redwood can support a narrowly scoped, auditable SLA exclusion for cases where the content-policy pipeline (synchronous call) materially adds tail latency and causes downstream tool-call timeouts. We don't do broad carve-outs, but we can agree to a limited operational exclusion with explicit guardrails:

Proposed next steps (quick):
- Ben to provide a short technical assessment and proposed mitigation (local cache / async fallback).
- We'll draft a 90-day timeboxed SLA amendment that:
  * Defines the exact trigger conditions (e.g., policy-check > 850ms, tool-call timeout event).
  * States that requests matching the trigger are excluded from the per-request latency SLA but are subject to availability SLAs.
  * Requires automated alerts and a shared dashboard to FinPay with the incident stream.
- Karthik will sign off on auditability requirements and evidence needed for security approval.

I attached a one-page proposed mutual action plan (proposed_map.xlsx) to keep the procurement thread moving. Can you confirm FinPay's preferred rollback triggers (e.g., X incidents over Y hours) and whether a weekly sync works for the first month?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for filter-triggered toolcall failures — technical readout

Hi Liz,

Thanks for the logs. Quick technical readout from the SE side:
- Root cause: the content-policy component (third-party policy engine) is currently called inline before the structured-output tool-call. When the policy engine experiences tail latency, the overall request hits the service-level tool-call timeout (configured at FinPay client to 2s), leading to failed transactions.
- Frequency: these events are rare (~0.6% of requests at peak) but cluster under peak traffic bursts and for certain prompt patterns.

Technical mitigations we recommend (short/medium term):
1) Cached verdicts (best-effort): maintain a short TTL cache of recent policy verdicts keyed by prompt fingerprint. When the policy engine latency exceeds threshold, return cached verdict and dispatch a background rescore.
2) Async rescoring/fallback: allow the tool-call to proceed with a conservative fallback policy and queue the full policy check asynchronously; if async check fails post-hoc, emit an audit event and optionally rollback in the orchestration layer where possible.
3) Defensive timeouts and retry: increase client-side tool-call timeout to 3s with a single fast retry for transient policy latency spikes.

Acceptance criteria for a scoped SLA exclusion:
- Exclusion applies only when policy-check latency > 850ms and the request would otherwise hit the configured tool-call timeout.
- Exclusion limited to the FinPay integration domain (account-specific).
- Redwood will provide a dedicated dashboard and an incident stream with per-request tags for any excluded events (JSON event ids).
- Both sides will define rollback triggers: default proposal = >15 excluded events in a rolling 24h window or >0.5% of requests in a 7-day window.

I've sketched a short tech note attached (tech_note_filter_pipeline.md) with pseudocode for caching and background rescoring. We're prepared to pilot the change in a canary region and share metrics.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: tech_note_filter_pipeline.md (text/markdown, 9KB)

Cc: procurement@finpay.com, security@finpay.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for filter-triggered toolcall failures — FinPay position

Thanks Ben and team — that readout helps. FinPay is willing to accept a narrow, timeboxed operational exemption under the following conditions:
- The exclusion period is 90 days from the effective date with a possibility to extend by mutual agreement.
- Redwood provides a live dashboard and daily digest of excluded events and the JSON event ids for cross-correlation.
- If rollback triggers (the ones Ben proposed) are hit, Redwood must revert to strict policy gating within 4 hours and notify FinPay’s security team immediately.
- FinPay requests a one-time service credit for the three incidents in May that materially impacted customer flows; procurement needs a short justification to include in the amendment.

We can do weekly 30-minute tech syncs for the first 4 weeks. Procurement is ready to review a draft amendment and DocuSign link.

—Liz
Liz Harrison
Head of Integrations, FinPay Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harrison <liz@finpay.com>, procurement@finpay.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment draft + next steps (FinPay)

Liz / procurement team — thanks for the quick alignment. Attached is a draft SLA amendment that captures the operational exclusion language, monitoring commitments, rollback triggers, and the one-time credit proposal.

Summary of key terms (draft):
- Scope: Exclusion applies only to FinPay account requests where the synchronous content-policy check exceeds 850ms and causes a tool-call timeout.
- Duration: 90 days from effective date (auto-expire unless extended in writing).
- Monitoring: Redwood to provide a shared dashboard with per-request flags and a daily digest; event ids included.
- Rollback triggers: >15 excluded events in rolling 24h OR >0.5% of requests excluded over 7 days — auto-revert to strict gating and notify FinPay security within 4 hours.
- Credits: Redwood to apply a one-time credit equivalent to 3 days of average hosted usage fees for the month of May 2027 for documented incidents.
- Evidence & Audit: Redwood will produce a weekly summary of excluded events and provide the underlying logs for audit within 5 business days on request.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review the attached PDF and confirm DocuSign recipient and billing contact.
2) Engineering: Ben to schedule a canary rollout and share dashboard link.
3) Security: Karthik to confirm audit package and required retention window.
4) Weekly sync: propose Mondays 10:00am PT for the first 4 weeks — please confirm.

I put the draft in DocuSign and HubSpot (links below). If procurement confirms, we'll route the amendment for signature and schedule the canary.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
